Tall Boy Is a Stand-In Teardrop Trailer That's Cheap, Light, and Highly Modular
14 photos
Photo: Bend Teardrop
In a world of ultra-compact teardrop trailers that barely fit a double mattress inside, the Tall Boy makes for a surprising – and welcome – appearance. A teardrop that offers full standing height inside and accommodation for as many as five people depending on configuration, this trailer is what you could – and should – consider a must-see.
Tall Boy is the newest addition to the catalog of boutique-style Oregon-based Bend Teardrop, but it's not new. It debuted as a concept in late 2023 and made its way on the market in the flesh metal in February of the next year.
Since then, it's been a staple with this particular manufacturer and a hit with the customer base. Once you take into account all the pros working in its favor, it's not difficult to understand why. After all, the first thing that comes to mind when you say "teardrop trailer" is not the ability to stand up or a surprising degree of modularity.
And that brings us to the hottest selling point of this model, which has been refined constantly up to 2026: while still lightweight enough to be towed even by smaller vehicles and even moved into position by hand, it's tall enough to offer comfort comparable to a full-size travel trailer.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Tall Boy is built on the older Double Family model chassis, so you're looking at 16.5 feet (5 meters) of overall length, 7.1 feet (2.1 meters) of wheel-to-wheel width, and 8.3 feet (2.5 meters) of total height. That last one allows for 6.3 feet (1.92 meters) of interior headroom, so you can fully stand up inside.
A purist would argue that, despite the official description, Tall Boy is not a teardrop but rather a very compact travel trailer or, at best, a squaredrop . A purist would be right, but let's not let semantics get in the way of a nice product.
Tall Boy sits on a heavy-duty CNC-machined steel overland chassis, equipped with a single axle with spring leaf suspension. Construction is with an aluminum skinned shell, composite flooring, an aluminum-lined undercarriage, and an all-natural wood interior. Also standard, you get a pair of tinted slider windows and a couple of portholes, as well as a full-size entry door with a screen door.
Photo: Bend Teardrop As explained in the video tour at the bottom of the page and stated proudly on the official page, each Tall Boy is "built to suit." With a focus on an affordable edge over products from the competition, it comes standard with pretty much everything you need , but you can also customize it to whatever extent you want or can afford.
For instance, you can add independent suspension and beefier tires, or even an articulating hitch. That said, these upgrades will add to the cost of the final build, which will no longer be legitimately affordable.
You still have plenty to work with without the added expense, especially since this trailer is imagined as a family-friendly option that will either live at campsites or do mild boondocking – and little to no hardcore overlanding. Just for the interior, for example, you have four configurations possible.
Photo: Bend Teardrop You can choose bunk beds in front of the entrance with either an east-to-west double bed at the back or a California king that collapses into a couch during the day. You can add a removable table and you have dining and lounging taken care of. You can opt for either of these double beds and have a dinette instead at the front.
Depending on how you combine these, you can sleep up to five people inside, while still have some free floorspace to move around. The best part, according to the manufacturer, is that you also get storage for all these people, including under the two beds on the ground level.
Standard features inside include LED lights, power outlets and USB plugs, and you can opt to add more or change their standard location to suit your exact needs.
Photo: Bend Teardrop At the back, you get a sizable but basic tailgate galley . With the idea that everything has to be simple, affordable, and durable, Bend Teardrop puts here a stainless steel sink with a 2.5-gallon (9.5-liter) jug of water (you still have a faucet that will run city water if you hook up the trailer) and storage on a three-level arrangement.
This way, you get well compartmentalized storage, including a removable cutlery tray and a three-bottle built-in shelf. It might not seem like much, but it's the kind of thing that adds actual functionality to a space.
You also get 5.2 cu-ft (147 liters) of storage under the counter, where you also have space and a 12V plug for a cooler fridge. The extra large opening tailgate acts as weather protection, and you can add a separate hatch like the one in the unit below, for quicker access to the space under the counter.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Tall Boy "comes loaded" by default, in the sense that it's ready to go from the moment of delivery. By that, Bend Teardrop understands 200W of solar on the roof, trailer brakes, a 2-inch receiver hitch, AC shore power hookup with charger, the full door with lighted fold-out steps, a pass-through compartment at the back, a 10-speed two-way powered vent, a slide-in manual awning, and the upgraded galley.
Optionally , you can tweak just about everything, add a roof-mounted or a portable AC, a heater that will sit inside the pass-through storage compartment, a 12V TV, and a storage box or rack on the tongue. You can also have the manufacturer install a bike rack or further switch things up with the interior.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Whatever you add (or don't), the interior will be cottage-like, with real wood finishes on the walls, ceiling, and cabinetry.
The standard Tall Boy comes in at 1,995 lbs (905 kg) of dry weight, with just 150 lb (68 kg)of tongue weight, and a price of $22,950, which Bend Teardrop says is affordable given the kind of value and the quality of work you get.
